## 2026-09-18 — W16H: the note was right, the advice was not

The twelfth Astra-medium calibration scored 85 with `scale_and_limits` at 65 on
a 54,982 ms cold first feed. Measuring it (`0f4ff08e98`) ruled out acquisition
volume and left one table: `follows`, `sync public`, no horizon, ~1.7 MB of a
6.7 MB cold acquisition for one persona.

Detection was not the problem, and I want that on the record because the
temptation is to read this entry as "the diagnostics are noisy". They are the
opposite. That builder declared 17 `sync` lines, 12 unhorizoned, and `check`
emitted exactly **one** `N_NO_HORIZON` — on the table that mattered, on every
check they ran from first to last. The suppression rules did their job exactly.

What the one correct note said was `rewrite: sync public last 500 by byPair`.
`byPair` is `follower, target`: no time order, so that horizon keeps the 500
alphabetically-highest pairs. For `sync public` the group prefix is empty, so
`columns().starts_with(&prefix)` held vacuously for every index and the
`BTreeMap` returned whichever name sorted first. Renaming `byTargetTime` to
`aaTime` — changing nothing else — changed the recommendation, which is now
pinned as `w16h_horizon_advice_does_not_depend_on_index_name_order`. I ran that
test against the base first and watched it fail with
`left: "sync public last 500 by byPair"` / `right: "sync public last 500 by
aaTime"` before trusting it; a regression test that has never failed is not
evidence.

The part that decided the ranking: applying the note's own rewrite verbatim
gives `check: ok — no problems` and the note disappears, and the semantically
correct horizon gives the identical verdict. Static compilation cannot tell the
two apart — both are well-formed — so there is no downstream gate, and the
advice string is the only place in the toolchain where this can be decided. A
builder who follows it is paid a green check for making the app worse. That is
a better reason to ignore diagnostics than noise ever was.

Built: an index qualifies as a horizon only if the column after the prefix is
minted in time order — a `time` column or `id`. Admitting `id` is load-bearing,
not a convenience: it is what keeps `sync to members[.conversationId] last 500
by byConversation` correct, the paved horizon in the corpus. For `follows` every
index leads with a `principal`, so nothing qualifies and the advice falls to the
branch that says to add the ordered index first — a branch that already existed
and was, before this, unreachable for any table with any index at all.

Two smaller ones travelled with it. The builder wrote `cap 1000 by follower` on
that table: they had already tried to bound it, and the cap is over `follower`
while the sync group is the public partition, so it bounds nothing a device
acquires. Capped and uncapped schemas produced byte-identical notes, which reads
from the author's chair as advice that has not noticed what they did; the note
now names the cap and says what it does not bound. And every note now names
`check --residency`, which already reports acquired bytes per table per persona
— the ranking the note itself cannot carry, and which no builder in the
programme has been observed to run.

Separately, `schedule … every 30s` answered "a period is a number and m, h or
d". But `s` is a real Quarry unit — work durations take `s m h d`
(`parser/actions.rs`), route waits take `ms s` (`parser/routes.rs`) — so naming
the valid set alone reads as "`s` is not a unit" and hides the actual rule: a
schedule cannot fire more often than once a minute. That floor lives in the next
branch, which a sub-minute unit returns before reaching. The message now states
it, modelled on the route-wait message, which already states its range and was
the best of the three.

Verified rather than assumed: the new test fails at `a8de12ed88` and passes
after; all 40 `residency_notes` tests pass; the cal12 builder's real table now
yields `by byAt: at, id  -- then: sync public last 500 by byAt`, identical under
the rename, checked against a built binary and not by reading the source; a
valid `every 1m` schedule still parses past that line; `ref-check --verbose` is
ok at 9,116 refs.

Two of my own errors, caught before they cost anything. I wrote an `@ref` to
LLP 3000.007 §20.23 when §20.22 was the last section — the reference was to a
section I had invented, and `ref-check` would have refused it in CI. The repair
was to write §20.23, not to delete the annotation: what qualifies as a horizon
index is exactly the kind of decision the corpus exists to hold. And I passed
`&&Index` where a closure wanted `&Index`; method calls auto-deref and closure
arguments do not.

One claim I am not making. I started to write that three consecutive builders
ignored this note. cal10 and cal11 have no `follows` table at all, so that was
false, and I removed it before it reached the ticket. What is true is narrower:
one note, one table, the right one, ignored — and the advice attached to it
would have made the app worse if taken.

## 2026-09-18 — W16H/2: the worker entry sits one directory outside the ESM island

The 0.2.28 builder wrote, of this: "the conventional worker entry and Node module
mode produced avoidable setup loops", and in the diary, "**agent mistakes, not
demonstrated backend defects**". They took the blame. The log does not support
that, and `setup_and_docs` — 96 → 88 fitted over ten runs — is the category it
lands in.

`evidence/backend.log:175-195`, seven times: `snapback4 worker: .../server.ts`,
then Node's `Failed to load the ES module`, `SyntaxError: Cannot use import
statement outside a module`, eight frames of `cjs/loader`, and
`exited exit status: 1; restarting in 250 ms`.

`init` is right in intent and I want that recorded before the defect: it does
**not** force the application to ESM. It preserves the project's module type
(`inherited_package_type`) and gives the code it generates its own island —
`snapback/generated/package.json` is literally `{"type":"module"}`
(`project.rs:280`, `@ref §20.2`). The island is `snapback/generated/`. The
documented author entry is `snapback/server.ts`, one directory above it, so it
inherits the project's type while the generated code beside it does not. The
guide's example for that very file is ESM (`guide/actions.rs:35`,
`guide/routes.rs:36`), and `"type": "module"` appears nowhere in the guide, the
README or SERVER.md.

`dev` already gates the entry twice and gates it well — `E_SERVER_TOOLCHAIN`
names `bun add --dev typescript @types/node`, `E_SERVER_TYPECHECK` prints the
compiler's own line — and forty lines further into the builder's log,
`E_AUTH: this is a worker's door: send a live service token (`snapback4 token
--service <name>`)`. Typecheck cannot see module resolution, though, so the file
passes every gate and then fails to load. At that seam Snapback said
`exited {status}; restarting in {} ms` and forwarded Node's trace.

Built: before spawning, if the entry is `.ts`/`.js`, carries a top-level
`import`/`export`, and no `package.json` above it declares `"type": "module"`,
name the repair.

```
snapback4 worker: …/snapback/server.ts uses ES modules but the nearest package.json
  does not declare them, so Node will read it as CommonJS
snapback4 worker:   rewrite: rename it to server.mts — or declare "type": "module" for it
```

Advisory, not a refusal: Node still gets its attempt, so a loader or a future
type-stripping default cannot be locked out by a heuristic of mine.

Verified by running it, on a probe reproducing the builder's configuration
exactly — root `"type": "commonjs"`, `snapback/generated/package.json` present,
their own `tsconfig.json`, an ESM `server.ts`. It reproduces their failure
verbatim, and the advice now precedes the trace. Both negative controls are
silent: `server.mts` (the fix they reached unaided), and `server.ts` in a
`"type": "module"` project. `cargo test -p snapback4`: 265 tests, 10 binaries,
0 failures.

Two judgements worth stating. The first message I wrote spelled the rename as a
full absolute path; in a lane whose entire subject is that advice must be
usable, shipping that would have been self-refuting, so it names the file the
way the author would perform the rename. And I did **not** change the guide's
documented example to `server.mts`, which is the change that would actually have
saved this builder: it moves a paved spelling across the corpus, and with the
remove-vs-document question unruled and cal13 in flight, that belongs in a blind
round rather than in a unilateral edit. It is recommendation 1 of the ticket,
left open on purpose.

The wider point, and the reason this sits beside §20.23. The builder blamed
themselves. The wave-13 session independently found the same shape in the bounds
bar: the one loop that repeats — guessing a root `snapback4` export and the
bare-arguments wire body — was paid by six builders of seven, **every time
self-attributed as agent error**. A calibration that reads builder
self-assessment is reading a floor on Snapback's share, not a count of it.

## 2026-09-18 — W13jR1: name the starved shape when an earlier read spent its meter

Base: `a69cb6f771e01a6690e9afe36730701a02539938`; left uncommitted for the lead.
The review found that `meter.capped_at` preserves the first exhaustion site,
which can precede the returned shape. The refusal then called that earlier
read the shape and claimed its cost was the shape's own. The runner now records
one boolean on a trimmed shape position: whether the meter was already capped
before that row's shape ran. At publication it selects the zero-finished-row
shape whose source page owns the continuation, using the same predicate as
before. An inherited cap names that source read and the earlier exhaustion
site; a cap inside the shape keeps the existing own-cost message verbatim.
The ruling 35 reference remains at the publication check (LLP 3000.007#14).

Inclusive-candidate detection, token equality and the zero-finished-shape
condition are unchanged. The source scan, shape mark, starvation detection,
trimming positions, lane charges, device horizons, page planner, client,
ceilings and serialized forms are unchanged. The reads card and the registered
code's explanation gain the inherited case; the README's sentence remains
accurate and is untouched. The additional runner/shaping state is private,
not a wire or persisted value.

The new shared test runs on the server, memory device and SQLite device.
It uses the inherited-cap fixture's unconditional 9,000-row count, both range
and list lane sources, and both eager and lazy merges. All 12 inherited-case
executions preserve the first request: 0 returned rows, `complete: false`,
`cut: 'meter'`, and an inclusive cursor at row `a`. Each follow refuses with
the exact inherited diagnostic. The 12 positive controls bound the prelude
count to 3 against the same 9,000 rows: both pages return their row and its
2-row preview, without a meter cut or refusal, and the second has no `next`.
The bounded prelude count itself is truncated, so the query correctly stays
`complete: false`. The first post-fix test run mistakenly expected that
control to be complete; its assertion was corrected to require incompleteness.
No existing assertion was changed. The existing self-exhausting fixture's
exact message and first-request assertions remain green on all three hosts.

The inherited fixture before the fix, and the own-cost fixture both before
and after, have this exact refusal message:

```text
E_SHAPE_EXCEEDS_METER: the returned shape at programs.feed.1 examines more than the 8,192-row meter on its own; bound it (`first N`/`last N`) or move it out of the returned shape
```

The inherited fixture after the fix:

```text
E_SHAPE_EXCEEDS_METER: the returned shape at programs.feed.0 cannot finish: the 8,192-row meter was spent at programs.feed.1 before it ran; bound that read (`first N`/`last N`) or move the shape out of the returned shape
```

## 2026-09-18 — W13k: acquire the current readable rows (ruling 36)

Implemented the revision-3 lane design on base
`629ae76ec813ad06ec4cfb777a654e30733d23d9`. An acquiring, currently open join
now scans the current group in descending order at the serving transaction's
fixed clock, applies the joining principal's server read rule, and stops at N
readable rows without looking past the Nth. The full Nth key is the floor;
fewer rows, including zero, produce `whole`. Horizonless joins acquire every
current readable row. Closed joins acquire nothing, including uniformly
readable rows with retained history. Continuous renewals expand no rows; an
expired predecessor's scope still precedes its replacement acquisition.

The cold snapshot shares that walk and principal read check; live aggregates
still use the system runner. Log puts are normalized before join expansion so
that an acquired image is checked and delivered once. Removed the historical
completion proof, unselected walk, delivered-set tracking, both storage methods
and implementations, and the old row-log index (dropped when existing SQLite
and Postgres stores open). Updated the published sync card, package README,
and the RFC's law, W13g history, and newest revision-history entry. No wire,
value encoding, meter ceiling, device implementation, or existing corpus case
changed.

The rewritten two-worlds tests retain payload and marker equality. Added the
Rust-constructed mixed-readable schema pair, deletion pair, 1,000 hidden rows,
empty readable group, current horizonless acquisition and closed private/public
joins, duplicate puts across ordinary and staged pages, subsequent deletion,
group move, expiry, below-floor update, and stable snapshot/stream floor equality.
Both native device stores and wasm are covered. Descending horizonless order
also required the existing paged-snapshot retention test to retain `n3` first
instead of `n1`.

What this taught us: choosing readable rows directly removes the historical
proof entirely. Physical work can still vary with hidden rows, but the wire
and boundary do not. The public explicit-audience form is admitted by the core
and still rejected by Quarry: the native tests construct that schema in Rust;
the public wasm test exercises the corresponding constructed backend and
scope/put application, not an HTTP-authored public-subset program. Private
wasm tests use the real HTTP server. The design's collision example lists
`[collision, p2]`; its descending-order law yields `[p2, collision]` because
those keys are 2,000 and 1,500, with the specified floor 1,500. The implementation
follows that law. There are no other known design contradictions.

## 2026-09-18 — W13kR1: renewal preserves the undelivered acquisition; cross-host witnesses

Addressed the two verified review findings on base
`e93b7eec9ad6a045dd078cdd1f720ebff42b426b`. Expiry-tracking spans remain
separate, but a grant retains its acquisition obligation through contiguous
live renewals. Starting at the join's own nonempty span, each edge must end in
a join, match the next span's start sequence, and commit before the preceding
expiry (or follow a span with no expiry). The chain must end open and unexpired
at serve time. Scope and expiry gaps break it. Renewal joins still expand no
content. A replacement's expired-predecessor scope precedes acquisition whenever
that replacement's chain is live, including when its renewal is on another raw
page. Edge commit times are fetched together for the joined groups, including
edges outside the current page. A same-commit grant/revocation acquires nothing.

The first fix passed the reported regressions; an added exact-expiry control
found one more composition within the same finding: the synthetic predecessor
at a watermark can have zero width and the replacement's start sequence. It
must not mask the replacement's own span. The chain lookup now skips that
zero-width span. The controls also cover two successive renewals, no expiry,
a scope followed by a same-sequence rejoin, an already expired terminal span,
and same-commit grant/revocation. What we learned: a span's lifetime tracks log
authority at each commit; closing that span for a renewal does not settle an
undelivered acquisition, and the watermark's synthetic predecessor is not a
new grant.

The cold, gap and revoke/rejoin witnesses run both with a horizon and without
one, with both joins on one catch-up page and split across pages. The cold
witness starts with no snapshot. The gap witness first proves the device holds
the row deleted during the gap, then requires its removal, the ordered scope,
replacement rows, marker and local completeness. Both native stores and wasm
apply the same Rust-generated server pages. Expiring audience memberships sync
to the viewer so the device's independent expiry read check has its authority.
The existing snapshot-first continuous-renewal test remains unchanged and green.

Extracted the existing Rust mixed-readable fixture without weakening its
server assertions. Its actual stream and paginated snapshot pages now reach
SQLite, MemoryStore and wasm: 0, 1 and 1,000 hidden rows, a deleted historical
candidate, and empty readable groups with 0 or 1,000 hidden rows. Each host
checks the rows, persisted floor and completeness: at the Nth readable key is
complete; below it is incomplete and unknown; an empty readable group is whole.
The two-worlds wire and local-observation equalities remain. Quarry refuses the
mixed public read rule, so the fixture constructs that schema in Rust after
installing the admitted public schema; it does not relax schema admission.
The wasm suite invokes a Rust test exporter into a private temporary directory;
there is no checked-in generated fixture, new script, or production export API.

Parameterised the existing wasm duplicate/change witness over ordinary and
`retain delivered-history` tables. Added ordinary/staged witnesses in which
an acquired row moves below the floor before its insert and two later writes
are streamed. All three puts carry that same current below-floor image, leave
one stored row, and preserve the original persisted floor. The retained staged
combination is now explicitly exercised. Updated the README and sync card to
state that renewal preserves an acquisition not yet delivered. No diagnostic,
wire/value encoding, meter ceiling, selection walk, device implementation,
existing corpus case, or RFC section changed. The specified floors and earlier
W13k deletions stand. No out-of-scope file was touched; no commit was made.

Measurements: wasm is 1,595,051 bytes raw and 467,476 bytes gzip on both the
base and final builds, a 0-byte delta in each. The existing budget advisory is
15,476 bytes above 452,000; it is unchanged, not a new build failure. There are
13 renewal scenarios per host (26 native tests and 13 wasm tests), 12 generated
mixed fixtures per host, and 4 below-floor duplicate scenarios (retained/plain
crossed with staged/ordinary), each applying 3 duplicate puts to 1 stored row.
Horizon acquisition delivers 2 content rows; horizonless cold acquisition
delivers all 3; the replacement after gap deletion delivers 2. Renewal itself
adds 0 content rows and 0 markers. The cold/gap streams use 1 or 2 pages;
the split revoke/rejoin stream uses 4. The marker pair exists only for a
horizoned table; horizonless acquisition retains its existing marker-free wire.

## 2026-09-18 — W13kR2: same-commit joins carry (seq, ord)

Fixed the second review's High on base
`0f2e290bc271bf3c5796616689b752af0912d758`: joins sharing a commit were
mistaken for each other. Each interval now records the ordinal of its opening
join and the full `(seq, ord)` of its closing transition. The synthetic
watermark predecessor has no opening ordinal, so it can precede a real join
but cannot be selected as that join's own span. A real zero-width grant span
remains the start of its chain when it ends in a continuous renewal. Chain
edges match the next join's exact position and must precede expiry; scope and
expiry gaps break them. Only the immediate predecessor ending at the served
join's `(seq, ord)` decides whether it is a renewal or needs an expiry scope.
The first join in each live chain acquires once, and renewals acquire nothing.
The retained `joined` metadata also matches the surviving join's ordinal, so
several joins in one commit do not repeat the held group.

Added shared generated-page fixtures for grant/renewal, grant/revoke/rejoin,
grant/two renewals, and a same-commit renewal followed by a distinct-commit
renewal. Each runs with and without a horizon, together and paginated, and with
and without delivered-history retention: 32 fixtures, 64 native tests across
SQLite and MemoryStore, and 32 wasm tests. The first three use successive
transitions in commit 2 at time 500; the grant's expiry is 1000 and its renewal
extends to 2000 (3000 for a second renewal). Catch-up runs at 1600 from watermark
1 after the posts were seeded. Revoke/rejoin uses a real insert/delete/insert
mutation; renewal uses successive upserts in one `seed_at` batch. A later
member put provides a real page boundary, and changes expiry again only in
the distinct-commit-renewal case. Same-commit transitions stay indivisible even
at raw limit 1; pagination yields 2 pages versus 1 together.

Each fixture checks acquisition rows and their exact sequence/ordinal, one
marker pair with the expected floor for a horizon, scope before the rejoin's
rows, persisted boundaries, and local completeness. Retained rejoin now has
no first acquisition to survive scope and turn the second boundary unknown.
The wasm horizonless read also follows its cursor to the third row. Horizon
acquisition delivers 2 content rows, with 1 beginning marker and 1 completion;
horizonless acquisition delivers 3 content rows and 0 markers. Renewals deliver
0 extra content rows and 0 markers. The existing single-join-per-commit controls
and all prior assertions remain. The source fixture includes exact-position
observations only in test data; no wire field was added.

What we learned: zero width in commit sequence space does not mean a span has
no identity or acquisition obligation. Event ordinals distinguish a grant, its
renewals and a scope even within one transaction; a synthetic predecessor must
be distinguished by the absence of an opening join, not by width. Updated the
chain annotation and the README/sync-card sentence to state the same-commit
rule. Selection, floors, device implementation, ceilings, value/wire forms,
existing corpus cases, the earlier deletions and the RFC text are unchanged.
No out-of-scope file was changed, and no commit, push, tag or publication was
made. No diagnostic code or diagnostic text changed.

Wasm was measured by `bash scripts/build-wasm.sh` on the base and after the fix:
1,595,051 bytes raw and 467,476 bytes gzip in both builds, delta 0/0 bytes. The
build's 452,000-byte budget advisory remains 15,476 bytes over in both runs.
This is measured on the named base, not attributed to an unverified predecessor.

`git diff --check` at the repository root. Node, wasm and reference commands
used `export PATH=$HOME/.volta/tools/image/node/24.18.0/bin:$PATH` first. Logs
are `/private/tmp/w13kr2-*.log`. Every new composition was red before production
code changed and green after. No unrelated test failure occurred. Per this
round's explicit instruction, the full `scripts/test.sh` was not run; the lead
runs it at landing.

## 2026-09-17 — Repair B, round 4: private publication and declared-prefix replay

The round-3 brief supersedes the original per-row Repair B proposal in LLP
3000.001: defer the page's effects, receipts and published watermark together,
advance a separate durable transfer cursor, and publish the accumulated effects
before the first safe page and its replay. Current readable images remain the
server's materialization policy. `images_at` and `committed_above` now carry the
two bounds through the real server/client/device path.

The separate 256-ID defect is guarded: sync captures an actual prefix of
unretired submissions, and publication durably excludes its undeclared suffix
from replay. Entries remain queued. New captures cannot widen an older
response's implicit declaration. Pagination remains with the open cap ticket.
B2a's durable predicted-write-set refresh is a separate success-arm change and
regression test.

Private effects fold through the ordinary event applicator under a rolled-back
savepoint, preserving marker/scope/history/media order while storing only each
row's last image or tombstone and the affected metadata. Installation rechecks
the acquisition boundary, including a scope followed by recreation losing its
old holding exemption. On server-store replacement, private receipt proofs
retire old-incarnation writes before the buffer is discarded. The row cost is
the distinct backlog, not the outbox, and continuous catch-up has no timeout.

The implementation, every changed file, exact predicates, reset audit and
verbatim verification are recorded in `repair-b-round4-report.md` and
`repair-b-round4-verification.txt`. The three counterexample files remain as
correctness regressions on both stores. This lane performs no git history
operation, publication, wasm/release build, whole/simulator suite, witness or
root generator. The supervisor owns integration and the governing LLP update.

no Wasm/release build is too broad. The prescribed full device suite internally

## 2026-09-17 — Repair B, review fix round 1

This entry supersedes the round-4 implementation description above where it
conflicts. Replacement pages use the ordinary publication predicate and remain
in snapshot staging until safe. An occupied ordinary transfer must drain before
a replacement starts; its effects and acknowledgements cannot be discarded by
snapshot promotion. Catch-up requests always adopt the device transfer cursor.
Legacy terminal responses without `images_at` can publish.

The replay exclusion bound is captured with the request, not read from the live
outbox at publication. Each request records its live declaration; interpreting a
reply without the echo is the only place captures are intersected, and successful
apply ends that capture window. Adoption retaining confirmed images preserves the
published replay guard and does not replay already published observations. A
reset discarding private effects cannot turn their receipts into retirement.
Row recording separates final presence from first-admission provenance, so a
privately acquired row can move below its floor without disappearing; deletion
and recreation start a new admission. Folded acquisition metadata is installed
before boundary checks. An empty slot does not load the boundary namespace.

## 2026-09-17 — Repair B, review fix round 2: durable publication lifecycle

The follow-up to `891041ddf` puts open/adoption, local clear and store
replacement through `reset_publication`. SQLite invokes it inside schema
activation; memory does the fallible cleanup before its infallible exclusive
installation and persists the complete call together. Retaining confirmed
images retains their published replay guard. Empty transfer cursors mean no
transfer in both request construction and publication status.

One immutable capture holds a request's IDs and bounds until apply consumes it
or a send revision abandons it. `FIRST_CAPTURE` and the first/latest intersection
are removed. The checkpoint's bounds-only capture remains readable. Deferred
metadata keeps its existing per-key layout but records prefix tombstones and
subsequent writes explicitly. Present rows require admission provenance; nested
recording savepoints are unsupported, and failed writes do not enter the delta.

Receipts carry their incarnation in the same outbox value. Older implicit
receipts bind before replacement clears that incarnation; replacement watermarks
cannot retire them. The optional field is omitted on unsent records, preserving
the existing byte-format regression. First-identity preflight detects actual
replacement but leaves initial publication to apply. Requests recover both the
snapshot catch-up mode and private transfer identity from staging. Apply returns
publication status with its touched tables, without a second fallible read.

Some packet-only hypotheses did not hold in the full code: namespace deletion
already worked on both stores; folding already installed preceding metadata and
rows; ordinary history and watch invalidation already ran; and unpublished
terminal pages already caused the transport to continue. The per-finding record
and complete command/mutation logs are local evidence under
`target/review-fix2/`. Twenty-one distinct Rust mutations and one TypeScript
mutation failed their intended regressions; affected mutations were repeated
after the compatibility correction, with source bytes restored each time.

| Durable value | Sole writer | Sole clearer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device:deferred:rows:*`, `meta:*`, `acks`, `cursor` | `deferred::stage` | `deferred::clear` |
| `device:deferred:identity` | `deferred::stage_identity` | `deferred::clear` |
| `device:declaration:capture` | `predictions::capture` | `predictions::clear_capture` |
| `device:declaration:first-capture` | Removed | `predictions::clear_capture` removes old residue |
| `device:declaration:published` | `predictions::publish_declaration` | `predictions::reset` when images go |
| `device:snapshot:through` | `Device::apply_publication` | `snapshot::clear` |
| `Queued.receipt_store` | `predictions::record_receipt` | `predictions::remove`, with its outbox entry |

`deferred::PREFIX` and the former `DECLARATION_PREFIX` select namespaces; they

## 2026-09-17 — Repair B, review fix round 3: resumption and capture authority

Capture sorts decoded submission numbers before deriving both declared IDs and
the replay interval, rejects duplicate numbers, and uses one pending limit in
creation and bounds-only recovery. Recovery refuses an inconsistent over-cap
prefix. A request capture also owns its echoed bounds; mismatches refuse.
Dropping images invalidates observations of those images, retaining their
sequence as send evidence. That independent execution proof survives a later
replacement without allowing it to resend a known old-store execution.

A send now abandons snapshot rows and their owner/cursor/revision keys in its
revision-advancing transaction. It retains the private identity needed to bind
the receipt. Transport keeps the published identity used by adoption separate
from the identity used to continue a private transfer. An empty acquisition
marker means no acquisition. Replacement recognizes a private incarnation even
before the first published identity and retires its matching known receipts;
only legacy rewind uses the published/private receipt cut. Foreign receipts
still cannot retire from a replacement watermark.

Deferred admission evidence upgrades when a later image qualifies against a
completed boundary, including when completion follows puts on the same page.
Marker-only pages persist evidence changes in the row delta. Later moves keep
the evidence; deletion/recreation starts fresh. Tests reopen between private
pages. Malformed terminal ordinary pages whose image head exceeds their cut now
refuse before staging. The prefix-delta test rolls back its recording writes
before installation, so it proves installation into absent keys.

The per-finding dispositions, mutation scripts/logs and verbatim requested test
outputs are local evidence under `target/review-fix3/`. The supervisor retains
integration and the governing LLP update. This lane makes no push, rebase, merge,
whole-suite, simulator, witness, repository-root-generator, Wasm-build or
release-build claim. Device tests use the existing digest-checked rescore
fixture; the command shim refuses an actual nested Wasm/release build.

## 2026-09-17 — Repair B, review fix round 4: slot disposal and incarnation lifetime

S1: ordinary publication now consumes the deferred bundle while installing its
images/metadata and returns only those installed effects' receipts. Snapshot
publication explicitly discards any superseded same-position bundle, including
its receipts. The existing guard still requires an ordinary transfer ahead of
the published cut to drain. A debug assertion checks the whole deferred namespace
is empty before the shared tail changes the watermark, records acknowledgements
or replays. The acknowledgement helper can no longer reach into a hidden slot.
The new regression covers direct and staged replacement, with reopen before and
after publication, and distinguishes a discarded receipt from one incorrectly
promoted over the replacement base.

S2: publication pending reads the existing acknowledgement record's presence,
which every deferred bundle writes even when its map is empty, plus snapshot
ownership. It no longer infers private effects from the request cursor. The new
regression independently varies cursor and slot, then publishes both nonterminal
and terminal pages. No new durable marker or wire field is introduced.

S3: generation installation preserves known private incarnation while clearing
obsolete transfer effects, for both open/adopt and keep/drop image policies.
Authenticated observation also remembers identity before first apply, because a
generation mismatch can cause adoption before the response is staged. A later B
response must therefore detect replacement of A, fetch/adopt B's backend even
when its generation equals A2, and retire A's execution receipts. The dispatcher
regression exercises all four lifecycle combinations on memory and SQLite,
refuses B's acquisition under A2, then confirms B's query program and an empty
outbox through two reopens. This round verifies the device/dispatcher lifecycle;
it does not claim to rerun the reviewer's TypeScript/native transport script.

The round 3 durable-key table's cursor, identity and acknowledgement rows are
superseded by these lifetimes: cursor is request progress only; ACKS is slot
occupancy and is consumed on installation or discarded on replacement; private
identity is also written by authenticated observation and survives generation
installation independently of effects. Published STORE_ID remains adoption's
comparison value. Replacement still settles matching receipts before clearing
the discarded incarnation's state.

The smaller findings were read in full. Three test weaknesses were strengthened:
count transaction opens to catch post-commit reads through a transaction, reject
wider declaration echoes, and seed every private bundle/snapshot member before
checking cleanup. The other Medium/Low diagnoses are disposed with full caller
and storage evidence in `target/review-fix4/dispositions.md`.

Nine independent mutations compiled and failed their intended regressions,
including both S1 disposal and receipt leakage, the S2 cursor proxy, S3 identity
loss and receipt retirement, and the three strengthened tests. Source bytes were
restored and their hashes verified. Scripts, failed-run logs and the per-finding
report are local evidence under `target/review-fix4/`.

Final requested verification: `cargo test -p snapback4-device` exited 0 with
**569 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored** (existing); `cargo test -p snapback4-core`
exited 0 with **160 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**. Verbatim outputs are in
`target/review-fix4/device.log` and `target/review-fix4/core.log`, also embedded

narrow shim which refuses actual nested Wasm/release builds; its SHA256 remains

## 2026-09-17 — Repair B, review fix round 5: cursor, request and identity lifetimes

The author corrected the legacy-wire rule: absent image-head/committed-ID fields
mean no deferral. Old servers retain the original double-apply limitation; holding
every replayable local write would wedge a live tail. LLP 3000.001 records the
correction. Terminal snapshots now share ordinary pages' no-gap validation, and
the deferral predicate independently excludes all terminal pages.

Live transfer progress precedes a terminal snapshot cut. Sends abort only paging
snapshots; terminal catch-up keeps its owner/cut and updates its send revision.
Private continuations require their request cursor and compare against that floor;
first replacements can start from zero. Snapshot catch-up cannot masquerade as an
identity-free ordinary rewind. Apply observes first identity privately and promotes
the page-or-staged identity only with publication. Row-only reset now preserves
known private incarnation; a same-generation replacement must adopt its own backend
and retire the discarded incarnation's receipts. Both-store dispatcher tests and
an HTTP/native transport test exercise A→A2→row reset→B through reopens.

Corrections to the round 3 durable-key table:

| --- | --- |

## 2026-09-18 — structural boundary sealed below handler branches

The server handler's `MetadataReply.recovery` holds an opaque `OverflowGrant`. Its fields and the writable byte counter now live in a nested measurement module, inaccessible even to new read/metadata branches in the surrounding file. ## 2026-09-18 — round 3 structural repair; criticals green

The four original critical tests now pass (`/tmp/f188-round3-green.log`, 4/4). Server `serve_sync_stream.rs` owns a private `OverflowGrant`, with no decoder or public constructor. Its only producer consumes `ResponseSize.overflow`, reached through the ordinary borrowed event serializer or exact `StreamReply` serializer at the unchanged ceiling. `MetadataReply` contains `Option<OverflowGrant>` with private fields: no outer discovery arm can set a grant boolean. The grant carries only the already disclosed store ID, generation and requested position.

Device `grant::Accepted` can only be produced from the received bound grant after position/lease validation; its method owns all recovery effects. Every grant requires `from == captured_watermark`, even with a live staged lease; the lease remains an additional check. This is compile-time construction discipline inside the trusted endpoints, not a cryptographic proof across arbitrary JSON or a malicious server.

Discovery now carries `after`, refuses omitted/empty store IDs, excludes the tip, observes foreign identities through the existing transactional identity operation, and gives generation/backend adoption precedence over grant consumption. Existing acquisition/renewal errors propagate Err, so the test intentionally injects the otherwise unmeasured None outcome rather than falsely claiming a natural join-error reproduction. Both red witnesses are preserved in `/tmp/f188-round3-red.log`; the independently resumed red run is `/tmp/f188-round3-resumed-red.log`. Both report 0 passed / 4 failed for C1/C2. Later positive tests call inspect_engine and deliver its actual grant to both device stores.
- **C2:** the staged-stream path is live; its equality exemption was dangerous. Removed that exemption. Every accepted grant requires from == the confirmed captured watermark, and a stream request additionally requires its matching live lease. The final C2 tests grow an already confirmed commit's current images, obtain a real server overflow grant at its obsolete from, and verify denial preserves device state, held query results and the lease.
- **Client position:** discovery and its device capture carry the exact after token; a snapshot continuation cannot ask for or accept stream recovery.
- **Client denial:** only E_STORE_RESTORE enters restore handling. The helper already guarded this internally; explicit caller classification and real-client stale-capture/read/retry tests now establish the behavior.
- **Omitted store:** absent or empty store_id refuses E_INPUT before discovery. An unidentified client may shrink ordinary pages but cannot use identity-free discovery.
- **File-backed measurement:** ordinary streaming and measurement share one catalog-validated read transaction and reply builder, including acknowledgements and fixed now. File-reader failure refuses rather than changing paths. Concurrent enlargement and shrink tests prove measurement stays with the pinned ordinary reply; real file-backed HTTP/client variants pass.
- **Adoption ordering:** generation/backend-required observation precedes grant acceptance. A fresh capture/request is required after adoption; outstanding adoption cannot consume a grant.
- **Store mismatch:** the captured metadata command observes replacement transactionally, retires only known writes, persists backend-required, invalidates host freshness before its queued device transaction, and reconciles media after reset. Metadata never enters row installation.
- **Tip:** eligibility requires from < watermark. The tip and snapshot cursors do not run measurement or grant recovery.
- **inspect_engine coverage:** both device stores accept real measured overflow; full-reply-only overflow, fitting prefixes/replies, identity/generation/position mismatch, stale readers, serializer error and incomplete inspection are covered.

The construction boundary is structural: the nested measurement module's opaque grant cannot be built or rebound by outer handler branches; the device's private Accepted value includes every recovery fence and borrows the exact transaction it will modify. It remains authenticated-server evidence across the JSON wire, not a cryptographic claim against a malicious server.

Open limits remain explicit: early current-image stopping is not an end-to-end traversal bound; generation adoption still uses the pre-existing program-only retained-history policy; in-memory discovery retains its already tracked writer-mutex contention (`issues/20260918-snapback4-in-memory-sync-measurement-writer-contention.md`). The web artifact is 415,730 B gzip, 4,730 B above the unchanged budget; device-diet owns it and no size repair was attempted. No ceiling, rule, card wording or disclosure boundary changed. No commit, push, tag or publication. HEAD is aac90114d; llp/** and NOT-DOING.md remain untouched, and the original journal bytes are preserved as a prefix.

## 2026-09-18 — Repair B lands: a confirmed image may not carry a write the acknowledgements do not

A sync page's events are cut at its watermark while its images are read at the
server's log head, so a relative update committed in between sat inside the image
and outside the acknowledgement, and replay applied it twice: a counter read 3
against a server that never held above 2.

The page now carries `images_at`, the server reports `committed_above` from the
same lookup that builds `acknowledged`, and a page whose images contain one of
this device's own replayable writes publishes **nothing** — row effects, non-row
effects, acknowledgements and the published watermark defer together into a
durable slot while a separate transfer cursor advances. The first page without
that property installs the accumulation, applies itself, moves the published
watermark, applies the accumulated and current acknowledgements, and replays. It
terminates by construction: `stream` raises `next` to `head` when `more` is
false, so a final page always has `watermark == images_at` and cannot defer.

Two proposed mechanisms were refused by the implementation lane before this one,
each with an executed counterexample on both stores, and both are kept as
regressions. Deferring per row by each entry's recorded write set fails because a
page can change what a replay writes. Deferring images while the watermark and
acknowledgements still advance fails because a prediction then retires before its
effect reaches the base. A third refusal found the 256 pending-id cap, which
drops acknowledgements silently and replays a write over its own effect
permanently — a pre-existing defect reproduced on main with no repair applied,
now guarded here by not replaying what could not be declared, and ticketed for
declaration pagination.

Seventeen review rounds across two model families found no counterexample to the
mechanism. What they did find, over and over, was one fact with two
representations, or a lifetime not bound to one request, one incarnation or one
publication. The rule that closed the second class is worth keeping: *nothing
fallible may run between an authoritative commit and the invalidation it
implies.* Both families returned READY on the final round.

Integration onto main was not free. Upstream's indivisible-commit snapshot
recovery deadlocked against the lane's refusal to replace while deferred effects
remained — the required drain is impossible for a commit that cannot stream — so
a replacement now atomically disposes of the deferred slot and its
acknowledgements instead of refusing, which is the branch the lane's own first
review had offered. The client's snapshot continuations request `from: 0` with
their `after` token, and overflow observation no longer turns an event cut into
false, durable restore evidence.

The wasm budget rises from 411,000 to 434,000 B gzip under the 2026-09-18
ratchet ruling. Measured 433,908 B against main's 410,459. Attributed by ordered
ablation: deferred slot and recording 10,824 B; capture/declaration 6,889 B;
restore evidence 1,654 B; wasm opening 1,218 B; shared remainder 5,550 B. 2,686 B
were reclaimed before raising. The remaining 23,449 B is about 21.3% of the
diet's recovered bytes and is tracked in
`issues/20260918-snapback4-repair-b-device-bytes.md`.

by byCount: value, id

```text
a maintain value index is a prefix of group fields, then value, then any remaining group fields, then id; fields cannot repeat
by byScore: value, hour, postAt, postId, id; id may be omitted only when every group field is present
```

Worktree `sb4/mc-prereq-51b7a134`, HEAD `0fdac3dfb`, initially clean. The
round is local-only: no commits, pushes, tags or publication; no LLP,
NOT-DOING, ceiling, rule, card-word or disclosure changes. One Cargo invocation
at a time. No wasm size work.

Read-only orientation: LLP 3000 (root), LLP 2000.000 §§6–8 (meter, partition
and fixed vocabulary), and current LLP 3000.007 §18.2 (horizon acquisition,
retained history, identity replacement and request-local fences) govern this
change. Preserve acquisition markers, serve-time selection and merged renewal
chains. No LLP update is authorized; decisions and evidence stay here and next
to the affected code/tests.

F1 confirmed in `handle`: metadata and nonzero/stream requests return early,
leaving the public default route to a separate snapshot handler that drops
recover/generation. Added HTTP regressions for explicit and omitted defaults
with recover true and arbitrary generation, against memory and file SQLite
server stores, before changing production code. Expected result: metadata
without row/reset authority. Existing result: a snapshot reply.

F3 trace: local.ts's `recovery.snapshot` is the result of the Rust device's
sync_metadata command, not the HTTP recovery field. The device checks the
request and durable state; it cannot independently measure server JSON that it
never received. Add actual-client fabricated-wire regressions and distinguish
that boundary from authentication of a malicious server.

F1 red: `/tmp/f188-round4-f1-red.log`, **0 passed / 2 failed**. Both actual
HTTP handlers returned `snapshot:true`, no metadata, for the default-position
recovery request carrying generation 999999. The replacement dispatches every
successful /sync response through an opaque Reply with private snapshot,
stream and metadata variants. recover requests enter discovery even without
metadata:true. Snapshot images, identity and acknowledgements now share the
same catalog-validated read transaction; file-reader errors do not fall back.

F3 baseline refusal regressions pass **4/4** (wasm and process): fabricated
grant before limit 1, and wrong position at limit 1. However, the client alone
computed the page-limit condition in capture.recover. A second regression
sets that derived bit true on the actual larger-page capture. Both real devices
accepted the fabricated wire grant and cleared acquisition: **0 passed / 2
failed**, `/tmp/f188-round4-f3-red.log`, each returning
`{"ok":{"backend_required":false,"reset":false,"retired":{},"send_revision":2,"snapshot":true}}`.
This is an unchecked client decision, so F3 is a real, narrower fourth instance.
The capture now carries the actual limit; Recovery::accept requires exactly 1
(missing defaults to 0 and refuses). Tests also cover missing, zero and larger
limits with an otherwise real measured grant. Measurement remains the server's
job; this does not make serialized evidence unforgeable against a malicious
server or a host that lies about every request input.

F2 ruling: a stream success cannot carry a grant: StreamReply has no recovery
field. All successes now come through private ReadReply variants inside opaque
Reply. MetadataReply.recovery requires measurement::OverflowGrant, whose fields
are private in that child module, with Serialize only (no Deserialize, Default,
or public constructor). ResponseSize::into_grant consumes the counter; only
Counter::write sets its private overflow bit. No handler-layer remeasurement is
needed. New actual-HTTP cases send recover:true with arbitrary generation
999999 at zero, nonzero and staged-stream positions (metadata flag both ways),
on a fixture where a real limit-1 request demonstrably overflows.

F2 replay qualification: the device checks the captured revision against durable
SEND_REVISION, not against a revision embedded in the grant (there is none).
A stale capture, changed position/identity/generation or consumed stream lease
refuses; the broader statement that every saved response plus any fresh capture
must fail is not established and is not the contract. This is authenticated
server evidence, not a signed or single-use wire token. The prior G2 test even
injects matching wire evidence to test receipt retirement; renamed its title
from “measured reset” to “accepted recovery” and explicitly documented the
simulation so it cannot be mistaken for a measurement proof.

Remaining findings: discovery no longer writes requested_watermark at all;
SyncCapture preserves requested from separately from captured_watermark. Every
data/metadata success obtains store identity within its read transaction;
foreign snapshot cursors reset to the first page, while stream/discovery return
the actual store for device observation. from == head is now covered through
the HTTP dispatcher on both stores. Error replies remain deliberately identity-
free: a separate read cannot bind identity to the failed transaction, and denied
has no reset authority. The data-only stage_snapshot flag keeps rows private
until catch-up; metadata control flow exits before apply, and the device enforces
identity, generation, send revision, snapshot owner/continuation and boundaries.

## 2026-09-19 — MC1 milestone zero: both devices adopt, gate 5 fails on page growth

**Gate 5: FAIL.** At **100,000 parents and 1,000,000 source rows**, activation
took **51.255 s**, peak RSS **24,100,864 B**. The separate stopped-store proxy
backfill took **2.798 s**, peak RSS **128,139,264 B**; together **54.053 s**,
not one atomic implementation. The current device adopted in **30.437 s**
and the lagging device in **32.954 s**. Both real SQLite process devices
finished at **generation 2, watermark 208**, with **100,000/100,000** parents
persisted at `likeCount = 10`. Their whole-lifetime peak RSS, including initial
acquisition, was **110,198,784 B** and **80,166,912 B** respectively. The HTTP
serving process peaked at **160,563,200 B**, separately from activation.

The large pre-activation page was **16,744,164 B**, below the unchanged
**16,777,216 B** ceiling by **33,052 B**. Adding the integer field adds
**60,000 B** across its 4,000 events: **16,804,164 B**, an excess of
**26,948 B**. The real response becomes a **236 B `E_BOUND`**. MC0 carries
recovery; it does not make the no-oversize clause pass. Under the lane's
explicit stop rule, **no maintained-column implementation begins and the
lead's ruling is required**.

Record: [`benchmarks/runs/2026-09-19-snapback4-column-activation/`](../benchmarks/runs/2026-09-19-snapback4-column-activation/README.md),
including the two schemas, deterministic fixture generator, stopped-store
backfill, full compressed HTTP bodies, request sequence, raw resource and
row counters, and `rederive.py`. Base and measured product source:
`5df0d211a12ef3255a142685d064ae56d794aba3`, including MC0 and W15c. The debug
binary was rebuilt with `cargo build -p snapback4 --locked`; its SHA-256 and
Node 24.18.0 are recorded. These are loaded-host observations, not a
production performance claim: the host reached load 83 during measurement.

What was verified rather than assumed:

- The million persisted, non-expiring source rows really reference the
  100,000 parents ten times each. The backfill derives their counts rather
  than inserting the expected answer from the generator.
- The proxy adds a required `likeCount: int` with **no literal default**.
  Parent images are filled while the server is stopped, then ordinary
  schema activation validates and adopts them. No private maintain or
  mirror evaluator is prototyped; their performance is not claimed.
- The partition log remains at **108,000 events**, commits at **208**,
  throughout backfill and activation. This proxy does not implement the
  future maintained activation's always-touched commit. Generation alone
  causes the observed replacement snapshot when the clients explicitly sync.
- The lagging device really stays at watermark **200** behind eight
  pre-activation commits. Request ordinals **298–301** show `/sync` from
  200 at limit 4,000 returning `E_BOUND` with generation 2 and watermark
  204, then `/schema`, then the real device's successful `adopt` with
  watermark **0**, then `/sync` from **0** at the unchanged **4,000** limit.
  This is MC0's adoption-before-shrinking path; the refusal watermark was
  not applied. Every snapshot page fits, with a maximum of **16,764,471 B**.
- Each device makes **27 sync requests**. The current device has zero
  oversized replies and the lagging device has one. Both persisted stores
  contain every new total; direct device queries also return 10, fresh,
  with no server-query fallback. No source rows reach either device.
- Two successful post-activation half-pages reconstruct the oversized full
  page. Removing only `likeCount` and restoring the generation makes it
  exactly equal to the captured pre-activation page. Thus the added field,
  not unrelated row changes, causes the crossing. `rederive.py` independently
  reproduces the byte counts from the retained complete bodies.

The RFC finding is precise: LLP 3000.007.001 §3.11's event-free barrier avoids
one oversized activation commit, but does **not** establish §7 gate 5's
no-oversize clause for a pre-existing stream page. That page is still
materialized before the client learns the generation. MC0 correctly made it
recoverable and explicitly deferred a request-side generation check before
materialization. Commissioning that change or revising the gate needs the
lead's ruling; neither is silently substituted for the written bar here.
The separately owned newer-than-watermark prediction ticket is not made a
prerequisite, and no prediction or protocol repair is attempted.

in the device filename. The helper was corrected to encode the path and

## 2026-09-19 — W15b: provenance for public derived columns (ruling 31)

Base: `5df0d211a12ef3255a142685d064ae56d794aba3`. Implemented in
`snapback4-lang`; no engine, meter ceiling or serialized form changed.
The classifier was compiled through the existing integration test only while
running the first census; only after recording its hits and repairing the
published findings was it connected to ordinary binding. The temporary test
entry point is gone. No sub-agent, remote machine, commit, push or publication.

The proof is per written column, across Quarry programs, job preludes/chunks
and helpers in every catalog document. Program arguments carry argument
provenance through bindings, helper substitution, object/shape fields,
arithmetic and value-selecting conditions. Statement assignments track their
branch's control provenance; argument-dependent loop counts and conditional
breaks/continues taint carried assignments, and loop returns include their
selection provenance. Table and maintain reads supply read values; their selectors do
not taint those stored values. Ambient inputs are literals, `viewer`, `now`,
minted ids and presence (including `exists connected`). A column qualifies
only with a read-derived write and no argument, unknown or ambient-only write;
literal inserts and omitted literal/null defaults may initialize that column,
whereas literal updates/upserts defeat the proof. Upsert's implicit key writes
are included; an unresolved positional key is unknown rather than evidence.
Field-sensitive objects and shapes keep an unrelated argument out of a count's
provenance. A native job's arbitrary writes make the all-writers proof unknown;
a native query does not. Actions have no Quarry data-plane body; their external
steps' mutation arguments are already included. This is a conservative value
proof, not equality analysis or a claim that every derivation is recognized.

The existing public/uniform-read, provably unconditional insert/update rule,
immutable, append-only and maintain-target checks remain. The output stays one
`N_PUBLIC_AGGREGATE_COPY` note per column, `guide: feeds`, never a refusal.
Direct maintain copies keep their message. The rewrite now offers the maintain
or a source-pinning rule, with the absent count group's zero case. The card and
README's entire note section remain verbatim-equal and compile without notes.

Census counts include generated maintain targets and repeated table occurrences;
“blocks” means fenced blocks or source files. The corpus has 740 bundles,
782 files and 229 refused bundles, which cannot emit this note. Old hits were
measured with the base classifier. Broad-before-fix is the initial test-only
classifier on the original material; seven distinct presence-only false hits
were found across the first census and the control-flow regression pass.

and upsert, implicit upsert keys, native-writer uncertainty, message ordinals,
readOrdinal, editedAt, done, lastSeen, viewer-naming rules and jobs under deny.
The public pinning example executes zero and the true count successfully;
a forged existing row returns E_RULE. A forged absent upsert returns NOT_FOUND,
the existing absence contract, rather than §21.1's general E_RULE wording.

Whole-suite follow-up in this same entry: the first default blocking run
terminated with exit 137 without a summary; its cause was not established.
The second run used a dedicated temporary directory, four Rust processes and
serial client files. It completed the client inventory (884 passed, 1 failed,
3 skipped), but exposed two issues before its final collection. The stale
918-row delete/replace expectation now says 866, and all 30 init tests pass.
More significantly, three existing W13h finite-helper-composition cases did not
terminate: the new provenance loop fixed point repeatedly nested a JSON
`previous` field. I interrupted that run after isolating the three cases,
reproduced the compiler defect with a five-second regression, and fixed it.

A finite set of provenance bits is insufficient when its shape tree can grow.
The first iteration retains field structure; subsequent joins widen newly
growing subtrees to unknown, preserving their argument/read/ambient bits and
known sibling fields. Unknown defeats the column proof. This terminates the
analysis without a runtime ceiling change or a name exception. The focused
regression, existing simulator case and both device-store cases now pass.
The final census is unchanged. The validation below supersedes the earlier
source snapshot in this entry.

this appended journal entry, and one newest-first Revision-history bullet in
LLP 3000.007. The governing constraints are LLP 3000 §6–§7 and
LLP 3000.007 §14 ruling 31, §20.20–§20.21, §21.1 item 3, §21.3 P5 and
§21.6; §18's accepted decisions remain unchanged. No admission, program IR,
engine behavior, charge, ceiling, serialized value, code name or note severity
changed. No sub-agents, remote machines, clone, commit, push, tag or publication.
The existing P5 reference on the pass still applies. The published feeds/README
claim needs no change: these repairs make its existing propagation claims true,
and its verbatim-twin test remains green.

- **F1:** the pass validates builtin and helper arity itself, returns unknown
  for malformed/unsupported calls, and still visits writes in their arguments.
  Group/sort field selectors must be literal strings. Five malformed uncalled
  forms panicked at the reviewed commit; the regression covers called and
  uncalled `at`, `slice` and `group`, extra arguments, unknown functions,
  malformed selectors and a write nested in a malformed call. Called malformed
  helpers retain ordinary binding's diagnostic; uncalled helpers remain admitted.
- **F2:** a structural join visits each distinct field once, borrowing its
  children; influence walks the owned tree without cloning each subtree.
  Branches, iterations and merge lanes use scoped maps of changed bindings;
  untouched bindings are neither copied nor joined. Helpers are interpreted
  once per `(helper, argument provenance)`. Their column facts were already
  recorded by that first interpretation, so cache hits need no replay.
  Different argument provenance has a different cache entry.
- **F3:** slice bounds influence the returned container, its elements and their
  nested fields. Caller-selected positive/negative increments are silent;
  constant bounds preserve the positive read-derived control.
- **F4:** read-derived iteration cardinality influences carried assignments,
  including `total = total + 1`, which has no row field in its expression.
  That table-row count now gets the note; an ambient `range(0, 5)` count does not.
- **F5:** body results carry loop-exit influence out to the loop's join, including
  nested conditions. A caller's break after accumulation now silences the
  column; a read-dependent break remains a positive control.
- **F6:** two append-only derived insertions (the public log's
  `n: (last.n ?? 0) + 1` and a copied `p.score`) and a public write of a widened
  recursive JSON value assert silence. Each has an otherwise-qualifying positive
  control. Removing the AppendOnly filter makes its test fail. Replacing the
  widening summary with `READ` makes the recursive-public-write test fail.
  Both temporary faults were removed before final verification.
- **F7:** one 2026-09-19 Revision-history bullet names §20.21 and ruling 31.

Two brief clarifications were necessary without changing what binds. Quarry
has no `append only` declaration: that phrase produces `E_QUARRY_UNKNOWN`,
`unknown table declaration append`. `Constraint::AppendOnly` exists in the
core schema. The test attaches that existing constraint to a bound schema and
calls the production pass through a test-only path include, without exporting
an API or adding a declaration. The initial end-to-end 2,000-binding/2,000-if
query also exceeds five seconds in ordinary binding, independently of the
repaired pass. Its final timing test parses that same query, builds the catalog
and schema, and runs the production note pass directly, excluding ordinary
binding's type-environment copies. The deep-object query is timed end-to-end;
the repeated-helper case compiles a catalog containing an uncalled helper,
which this pass must inspect but ordinary binding does not inline. These are
provenance scaling measurements, not a claim about the entire binder's scaling.

## 2026-09-19 — W15b round 2: bounded abstract values and value-selection control

Continues `ef7bac6d7a` and `4ab1191008`; reviewed base for this turn is
`4ab119100889f815596a8283b862e3661cf674d1`. No commit, push, tag or publication.
This is the third appended W15b entry. The earlier journal bytes remain intact.
The scope is the optional `N_PUBLIC_AGGREGATE_COPY` pass, its existing aggregate
suite, the note's README/feeds twins, and the governing paragraph in LLP
3000.007 §20.21. No admission, IR, engine, serialized value, meter, ceiling or
existing conformance case changes.

F8 replaces owned recursive provenance with shared immutable nodes and cached
node counts/bit summaries. A value may represent at most **4,096 expanded nodes**
and **128 levels**; sharing does not discount its expanded size. Construction
checks the size before allocating its parent. Overgrowth replaces the whole
value with UNKNOWN, including field projections of an unknown root. The
**262,144 weighted-work-unit budget covers the entire catalog**, and therefore
each program within it, including helper calls, joins, influence propagation,
field construction, write-summary replay and control-flow traversal. The
traversal also has a **128-frame bound**. These are private diagnostic bounds,
not engine charges. Exhaustion abandons all column proofs: an unvisited writer
could invalidate any earlier note. The source regression deliberately exhausts
work after recording an otherwise-positive column and checks that no note leaks.

F9 records enclosing statement/expression conditions and loop cardinality in
write facts, including helper calls. A later break/continue also influences
preceding writes in that loop. The helper cache includes control provenance and
replays cached write summaries; merely remembering that a prior invocation
recorded them is insufficient when a later loop exit changes their context.
Short-circuit `and`/`or`/`??` arms carry the left operand's influence into helper
writes. Read control does **not** manufacture read evidence for `now`, `true`,
or a literal write. Return guards affect returned values, while a no-write
early return alone does not turn the remaining written value into an argument.
The literal insert/default identity exception remains valid under control.

F10 propagates every ascending/descending sort key into the reordered container,
elements and nested fields. Group keys similarly influence membership,
cardinality, `items`, and subsequent projections or sums. `first`, `last`, `at`
and `slice` preserve that influence. Unknown key forms remain UNKNOWN.

F11 found additional losses beyond the three review examples: optional shape
projection could discard the argument selecting whether a source exists;
short-circuit and conditional expressions could invoke writing helpers without
control; `group` could hide argument-dependent membership and a projected sum's
cardinality. Unknown table reads and rule-only `created` in uncalled helpers
could also supply bogus read evidence. All have silent regressions. Known
scalar builtins are enumerated explicitly; a future arity entry does not
implicitly gain the old optimistic scalar fallback.

### Expression and builtin audit

The table classifies the *provenance model*, not exact value evaluation. “Precise”
means the stated four-bit/field abstraction preserves the relevant dependence;
it does not claim constant folding or path feasibility. “Taints elements” includes
flattened summaries whose bits follow every later field/element projection.
Every row additionally falls back to UNKNOWN on a value/work/depth limit.
Read selectors intentionally do not taint stored values, as ruling 31's contract
requires. No note is an authorization proof.

| AST expression | Classification | Model / audit disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Name` | Modelled precisely | Local provenance; viewer/now/commit/new ambient; an unresolved name UNKNOWN. |
| `Focal` | Modelled precisely | Current row/element provenance. |
| `Literal` | Modelled precisely | Ambient; eligible as insert initialization only. |
| `Array` | Taints elements | Union of possible elements, preserving each field's bits; selection never drops a key's influence. |
| `Object` | Modelled precisely | Per-field provenance; unrelated argument fields need not taint a selected read field. |
| `Unary` | Modelled precisely | Operand bits; negative literal remains literal initialization. |
| `Binary` | Taints elements | Both inputs retained; list concatenation joins element shapes; other results conservatively flatten bits. Short-circuit arms propagate control to writes. |
| `Member` | Modelled precisely | Known field or whole-value summary; missing/unrepresented field UNKNOWN. |
| `Call` | Modelled precisely / conservatively UNKNOWN | Declared helper interpreted with arguments and control; cache replays writes. Recursive, malformed or unsupported calls UNKNOWN, while argument writes are still visited. Builtins below. |
| `Read` | Modelled precisely / conservatively UNKNOWN | Known table/maintain READ; connected ambient; unknown table UNKNOWN. Selectors traversed for writes, not mistaken for stored values. |
| `Merge` | Modelled precisely / conservatively UNKNOWN | Stored rows READ; unknown source table UNKNOWN. Lane/filter expressions visited. |
| `Exists` | Modelled precisely | The read's classification; connected remains ambient. |
| `Created` | Modelled conservatively (UNKNOWN) | Rule-only form, not valid program-value evidence even in an uncalled helper. |
| `Assert` | Modelled precisely | Preserves successful value; refusal is not another written value. |
| `Shape` | Taints elements | Per-field projection plus source selection bits; optional/unknown source cannot lose its influence when every field is replaced. |
| `ShapeUse` | Taints elements / conservatively UNKNOWN | Same projection model; missing or recursive named shape UNKNOWN. |
| `Walk` | Modelled precisely / conservatively UNKNOWN | Stored rows READ; unknown table UNKNOWN. Seed traversed. |
| `If` | Taints elements | Both possible values joined and recursively influenced by the condition; arm writes inherit control too. |
| `Write` | Modelled precisely | Patch/default/key facts and prior-image result; caller/unknown control disqualifies non-initializing writes, never supplies positive READ. Delete writes no column. |

The full core `Builtin` enum was checked against the Quarry lowering in
`bind/program/expr.rs` and `control.rs` and execution in `engine/runner.rs`.
IR-only spellings are named below so the audit does not imply a second Quarry API.

| Core builtin / Quarry form | Classification | Model / audit disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Calendar` / day, hour, bucket | Modelled precisely | Scalar summary retains all supplied input bits. |
| `Len` / count(text) | Modelled precisely | Text dependency retained. |
| `Slice` | Taints elements | Bounds influence container, elements and nested fields; text uses the same summary. |
| `Concat` / binary `+` | Taints elements | Both list-element shapes joined, or scalar union for text/identity forms. |
| `Lower` | Modelled precisely | Input summary retained. |
| `Trim` | Modelled precisely | Input summary retained. |
| `Sha256` | Modelled precisely | Input summary retained. |
| `Join` | Modelled precisely | List and separator summaries retained in text. |
| `Group` | Taints elements | Key affects membership/cardinality and every nested group item. Projected sum regression was red before repair. |
| `First` | Taints elements | Selected element retains container selection influence. |
| `Last` | Taints elements | Same; descending sort and group membership regressions. |
| `At` | Taints elements | Index and prior reorder/selection influence every nested field. |
| `Min` | Taints elements | Union of all operand bits, flattened so later projection cannot drop comparison influence. |
| `Max` | Taints elements | Same as min; caller-dependent scalar regression and positive read control. |
| `Divmod` | Modelled precisely | Both tuple components retain both operands' summary. |
| `Sort` | Taints elements | All literal key fields, stripping the descending `-`, influence every element/field; nonliteral key UNKNOWN. |
| `MentionTokens` / tokens | Taints elements | Text summary follows the result and selected tokens. |
| `DeterministicShare` / share | Modelled precisely | Amount, recipients and recipient summaries retained. |
| `Count` | Modelled precisely | Container/element summary retained conservatively, including grouped cardinality influence. No constant-length optimization is claimed. |
| `Sum` | Modelled precisely | Scalar input union; projection form includes container/cardinality and projection bits, with projected helper writes under that context. |
| `CountCapped` | Modelled precisely | Internal count lowering; same source provenance, not a separate supported call spelling. |
| `Connected` / connected[p] | Modelled precisely | Ambient presence, not stored-table evidence. |
| sorted(a, b) | Taints elements | Pair lowering to min/max; both names get the complete comparison summary. |
| range(a, b) | Taints elements | Loop-only form; both bounds influence cardinality and carried values/writes. |
| Unknown name, malformed arity, unsupported sort/group key | Modelled conservatively (UNKNOWN) | Explicit fallback; no automatic READ from a future builtin. |

Statement audit: binding preserves value bits; return joins value-selecting
conditions; expression/emit/require traverse their expressions and helper writes;
if scopes control, joins changed bindings and records conditional exits; for
widens carried bindings and applies domain and exit influence to write facts;
break/continue end the path and influence earlier/later loop writes. Require
and a no-write early return are successful-execution guards, not independent
sources of a written value. Literal insert initialization is the explicit
exception to disqualification, not read evidence.

### Measured bounds and regression evidence

The before experiment used the exact reviewed pass with test-only node counting
at object construction (no bounds, no provenance change). The two 200 ms
experiments ran separately so each timed-out test process exited with its worker;
no runaway background analysis was left on the shared machine. “Observed peak”
is the largest completed abstract value counted before timeout, not the final
required size or peak process RSS. The exact recurrence is `nodes(x0) = 1`,
`nodes(xN) = 1 + 2 * nodes(xPrev)`, so the unbounded x30 would require
**2,147,483,647 nodes**. That final allocation was deliberately not attempted.

| Exact 30-binding note-pass input | Before observed peak, lower bound | Before elapsed / 200 ms bound | Final peak expanded nodes/value | Final elapsed / 5,000 ms bound | Final weighted work | Widenings |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Unused helper | 262,143 | timeout at 205.039 ms | 4,095 | 1.352 ms | 16,797 | 2 |
| Called helper | 524,287 | timeout at 205.028 ms | 4,095 | 0.819 ms | 16,796 | 2 |

The exact unused helper also passes **full compilation in 0.319 ms**. The
exact called-helper measurement isolates parsing, catalog/schema construction
and this diagnostic pass, as the earlier sibling-branch stress test does. A
supplementary full-compilation probe, including a JSON-typed identity around
each branching object, exceeded five seconds (**5,001.485 ms**) in other
compiler work. That broader compilation bound is **not established** by this
lane and the attempted assertion was removed rather than weakening its time
limit. No change to ordinary binding or IR construction was made. This was
observed in the candidate; no independently base-verified attribution is claimed.
The targeted and language runs containing that attempted assertion each reported:

```text
test result: FAILED. 38 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 5.01s
```

The final whole-catalog exhaustion regression consumes **262,128** weighted
units before refusing the next charge, records **13 widenings**, peaks at
**4,095 nodes/value**, and emits **zero notes**, including the positive write
recorded before the exhausted helper. Three public-write controls exercise the
oversized value, a long field projection and an unknown-root shape. Existing
recursive-loop, 30-level join, 2,000-binding/branch and repeated-helper tests stay
green. Values widened by the node/depth bound carry UNKNOWN, never manufactured
READ. Shared pointers alone are not the claim: both expanded size and cumulative
analysis work have explicit bounds.
