## 2026-09-23 — 0.3 program: engine-recorded attribution (F2; LLP 3000.007.003 §3.2)

A maintain may key or filter by a one-hop reference path through an
immutable reference to a public target, for example
`maintain receivedLikes: count likes by postId.authorId`.

- **Capture.** At source insert, the engine records the target's value on
  the source row. The field is engine-only and engine-internal, named by the
  path, and never re-resolved.
- **Evaluation.** Incremental maintenance, expiry and rebuild all read the
  recorded value.
- **Activation.** Adding a path to a populated table captures once, with no
  row events, and devices reacquire. `doctor` reports null captures.
- **Load modes.** `Engine::load` has trusted-restore and untrusted-import
  modes.
- **Devices** predict only against live, covered targets, with coverage
  checked at the prediction clock through renewals and expiry.
- **Dotted aggregate keys** (`.postId.authorId`) are selectable on maintain
  targets.
- **Old versions refuse.** A new `Recorded` marker makes the published
  0.2.33 engine and device refuse F2 stores and backends, tested against the
  real published binary.

**Implementation.** An Astra xhigh lane on the Office M1 Max, with two fix
rounds.

- **Round 1:** Astra NOT READY. Its High: old engines and devices silently
  ignored recorded fields. Its Mediums: expired memberships authorized
  capture, and dotted keys were not selectable. Grok NOT READY on 8 of 16
  packets.
- **Round 2:** Astra NOT READY, with two Mediums: a membership renewal lost
  coverage, and an expired row masked its live replacement.
- **Round 3:** both earlier Mediums and the rebase onto the timeline code
  are closed. Its two remaining Mediums, an unmetered coverage scan and a
  bypassable missing-clock check, join the fix-forward batch
  (`issues/20260923-snapback4-readauth-and-f2-edge-cases.md`) that lands
  before 0.3.0.

**Integration.** Rebased onto `7877454ff` (READAUTH). Two additive conflicts
were resolved, both trait methods. The integrated suite on the M5 caught one
real break, a codec-census exception that F2's partition change had moved
out of its function; it was fixed at landing (census 26/26). Wasm is
465,589 B gzip. The ratchet rises to 466,000 because F2 together with READAUTH
costs about 1,800 B more than either measured alone.

The Office Mac was overloaded for much of this lane (load up to 158), with
two lanes running full suites at once. Per the independent review's advice,
fix rounds now run affected tests only, and the full suite runs once per
integrated landing.

## 2026-09-23 — exhaustive disclosure checking, and Kani on the key encoding

Charlie asked whether Snapback should use formal verification, and
commissioned two cheap trials before any Lean work. The first is exhaustive
small-scope checking of disclosure. The second is Kani on `key.rs`. The
simulator samples interleavings under seeds, but each of the 2026-09-12
reviews' disclosure findings needed one exact shape, and sampling rarely
produces one.

**Exhaustive checking (`crates/snapback4-sim/tests/exhaustive.rs`).**
The test enumerates every sequence of writes up to a depth against the real
engine. The cast is two viewers (`dev:alice`, and a principal named `public`
like the public partition), a stranger and two conversations. The chat
schema gains eight test mutations shaped like the reviews' findings:

- a grant that ends in its own commit;
- a grant and content in one commit;
- a grant replaced in one commit;
- two rows in one commit;
- three writes with no `require`, so that only the table rules stand between
  a viewer and a row.

A model of the chat rules, written in the test from the schema text and not
taken from the engine, judges each write. Every write the model refuses is
attempted at every state and must be refused without a commit. Every write
it admits becomes a branch, and its effect is checked. At every state, for
all three principals, the test checks the following:

- the snapshot is exactly the rows the rules admit;
- a stream requested from every watermark, at page sizes 1 and 1000:
  - delivers only current readable images;
  - labels none of them before the viewer's grant;
  - names no delete or scope for anything the viewer never held;
  - ends at the head;
  - applies the same rows at either size;
- every device schedule converges (bootstrap at any earlier state, then sync
  at any subset of the states since, at page size 1);
- `messageCounts` counts the messages;
- the write that reached the state, resent under its operation id, applies
  nothing new.

Depth 2 is blocking: 353 states and 36,818 refused writes in 4 s. Depth 3 is
opt-in: 7,131 states and 765,908 refused writes in 3 minutes on a loaded
Mac. Engine creation dominates the cost, at about 10 ms each, and SQLite's
allocator mutex serializes it, so the test uses two threads.

**One finding, metadata only:**
`issues/20260923-snapback4-in-commit-grant-names-ids.md`. When a grant ends
inside its own commit, the grantee still receives `scope` events naming the
group, and the group's members still receive a `del` naming the transient
row. No row image leaks, so the review's fix holds for content. The test
tolerates the finding by name and fails on anything else.

**Mutation proof.** Each hunk was reintroduced in the lane, the test was
run, and the file was restored byte-for-byte:

- **Untagged principal partitions (review finding 1): caught.**
- **No `scope` on revocation: caught** by three properties.
- **A commit split across pages (review finding 3): caught** by three
  properties.
- **An unchecked delete rule: caught.** `public` could unsend alice's
  message.
- **`append` not coalescing: not caught, correctly.** The stream re-reads
  current images, so for streams the coalescing is redundant.
- **At-most-once: never fired.** Removing the replay lookup, and then also
  the in-transaction receipt and the `_ops` key, changed nothing observable,
  because a further layer holds.

**Kani (`crates/snapback4-core/src/key_proofs.rs`, `scripts/kani.sh`,
outside `test.sh`).** Ten harnesses verified with Kani 0.68 on
`expo-build-450b`, from 4 s to 301 s each, all under 12 GB. This Mac, at load
80–130, starved them. Proved:

- over arbitrary byte strings of up to two bytes, text, id and byte bodies
  keep order and are prefix-free;
- `unescape` inverts `escape` whatever byte follows;
- every four-byte input decodes canonically without panicking;
- every `i64` pair orders and decodes;
- nulls, bools, ints and bytes of up to two bytes order and are prefix-free
  within their kind;
- the kind tags lead every key and sort in the value model's kind order,
  which decides every pair of different kinds.

Nothing failed a proof. What Kani did not finish became exhaustive unit tests
in `key::tests`:

- **Canonical decoding:** every input of up to three bytes (16.8 million).
- **Text and word scans:** every text of up to two characters over NUL, `a`,
  `b` and `é`.
- **Time scans:** boundary `i64`s, against every bound in both directions.

Two mutations of `scan_range` and `word_range` fail the scan test.

**Tooling fit.** The proofs themselves were quick to write. Making them
finish took about fifteen rounds, and each lesson is written in the proof
file's module comment:

- **A kind must be a literal.** A symbolic `Value` kind makes CBMC explore
  the recursive drop and comparison code of `Row` and `Map`, over
  `BTreeMap`s, and pass 40 GB.
- **So must a capacity.** `String` and `Vec` carry `Value`'s discriminant in
  a niche of their capacity, so a symbolic capacity, whether from growth or
  from a clone, is a symbolic kind.
- **So must a loop index.** CBMC does not fold one.
- **One heap payload per harness.** Several in one harness passed 40 GB.
- **No symbolic UTF-8.** Even one symbolic byte of text passed 40 GB inside
  `from_utf8`.
- **Scan proofs did not finish.** `scan_range` over a symbolic `i64` ran an
  hour without a verdict.

`--jobs` needs `--output-format terse`. The fleet runs used a watchdog that
stopped any CBMC above 40 GB, and it fired eight times. Kani fits pure
integer and byte logic, in seconds to minutes. It fits heap-shaped `Value`
code poorly. An exhaustive test over a well-chosen small alphabet gave the
same assurance for the rest in milliseconds.

## 2026-09-23 — 0.3 program: old engines and devices fail closed on 0.3 derived forms (FENCE)

The independent Astra review of the 0.3 program reproduced a P1: the
published 0.2.33 native device silently accepted a timeline-only backend. It
predicted only the application post, and answered Following `[]` with
`complete: true`. `Schema` has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so an ignored
metadata field is no fence.

- **One shared fence.** A schema that needs a 0.3 engine capability carries
  `Constraint::Capabilities`, a new enum variant that the published 0.2.33
  decoder rejects, in the device `Backend` decode and the engine's
  stored-schema decode alike.
- **Derived capabilities.** They come from the schema, never from the
  author: `recorded-attribution` and `timeline`. F1 adds `maintained-column`
  when it lands.
- **Strict 0.3 decoders.** They refuse unknown capabilities with
  `E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY`.
- **Kept backends validated on every opening.** Current devices check the
  kept backend's capabilities before replacing it, on explicit-backend
  openings too.
- **Legacy compatibility.** The legacy `Recorded` marker still decodes,
  including in combination with timelines.
- **Nothing else changes.** Capability-free schemas serialize exactly as
  before.
- **Tested with the published binaries.** Integrity-verified native and WASM
  builds refuse install, adoption and reopen for each capability. A
  capability-free control stays compatible, and downgrading a device below
  its store's version is documented as unsupported.

**Review rounds.**

- **Round 1:** Astra READY WITH CHANGES; an explicit-backend opening
  bypassed the kept fence. Grok found the legacy marker, over-claiming docs
  and a weak control test.
- **Round 2:** Astra READY WITH CHANGES; legacy F2+F3 stores could not
  reopen.
- **The integrated gate.** The full suite on EDGES+FENCE then caught FENCE
  regressions in device publication store-read counts and w13g boundary
  loading. Round 2 fixed them without extra store reads.

FENCE's own suite on the rebased tree (M5): `== 0 failure(s) in 676 s`.
Wasm is 466,824 B gzip against a 467,000 ratchet.

## 2026-09-23 — 0.3 program: four device edge cases closed before 0.3.0 (EDGES)

These are the Mediums left after READAUTH's and F2's third review rounds.
Each made a device refuse, hide or predict wrongly; none leaked.

- **Unknown coverage before meter exhaustion** now queues the mutation
  instead of refusing it.
- **Aggregate existence witnesses combine existentially,** so the result no
  longer depends on source-row order.
- **Coverage and witness scans are metered.** Device-only prediction work
  (coverage checks, provisional-row authorization) is charged to a separate
  device allowance whose exhaustion queues. Server-equivalent reservations
  stay on the mutation meter, so a device `E_BOUND` matches the server's.
- **Prediction clocks are validated:** `predict` refuses a missing clock,
  and a clock-less queued entry queues unpredicted.

**Review rounds.** Astra returned READY WITH CHANGES twice, first on the
device-only budget split, then on keeping reservations and metering witness
scans. The integrated suite on EDGES+FENCE caught regressions that the
affected-test runs had missed. The orphan-import tests failed because the
new clock requirement refused clock-less persisted entries; round 3 fixed
that.

**Landing.** Rebased onto FENCE (`7c655d652`). The integrated suite on the
M5 reported `== 1 failure(s) in 830 s`. The one failure, "a device restores
its session on its own", passes three of three when run alone. It flaked in
READAUTH's landing too
(`issues/20260923-snapback4-flaky-session-restore-test.md`). Wasm is
469,031 B gzip against a 470,000 ratchet.
## 2026-09-23 — rows and grants born and undone inside one commit log nothing

This closes `issues/closed/20260923-snapback4-in-commit-grant-names-ids.md`,
which the exhaustive explorer found. Charlie commissioned the fix, the
ticket's option (a). The rule is in LLP 3000 §7.

For each commit, `account_row_change` now tracks:

- the rows the commit inserted, in every table;
- the grants it newly made, where the partition or the group changed.

Each records the events it already had in the commit before its birth. The
rule:

- a born row logs only its image at the commit's end;
- a born grant stays born through renewals and expiry until it is undone,
  and undoing it withdraws its joins since birth and logs no scope;
- a replacement beside a pre-commit predecessor is not a birth;
- born siblings of one key share their birth.

**Review.** Astra reviewed blind, read-only, over five rounds
(`llp/reviews/3000-in-commit-grant-names-ids.astra.md`):

- **Round 1: NOT READY, three findings.**
  - A High: a re-created row erased its first deletion, which happens
    naturally for a maintained count.
  - A born row moved between recipients leaked a `del`.
  - A born grant lost its birth across expiry.
- **Round 2: a High present since the first version.** Undoing a replacement
  erased an unswept predecessor's revocation.
- **Round 3: a Medium.** A same-commit sibling was taken for a predecessor.
- **Round 4: a Medium.** Two born siblings shared one marker.

Round 5 was READY and saw no risk warranting another round. It named one
inherited Medium, a grant inserted already expired still naming its row and
group, now `issues/20260923-snapback4-already-expired-grant-names-ids.md`.
Every finding is a test in `snapback4-sim/tests/reviews.rs`
(eight new cases). Each fails on the version before its fix, and `churn` in
the explorer catches round 1's High on its own.

**A pinned behavior changed.** The W13g same-commit `rejoin` fixture
(`snapback4-device/tests/w13g_review/same_commit.rs`) and its JS twin
(`packages/snapback4/test/horizon-boundary.test.mjs`) pinned the old log
`join, scope, join` and one scope on the wire. The first grant is born and
undone in its commit, so the log now holds one join and no scope reaches the
device. Both are updated. All eight JS rejoin cases pass on the wasm device.

**Verification.** This Mac's load reached 190, so the complete Rust suite ran
on `expo-build-450b` from a copy of the tree:

- **Round-3 code:** the complete suite passed 811 targets. Its two
  50-minute device measurement tests (following calibration, search forms)
  were stopped, not completed.
- **The landed revision, rebased onto EDGES and FENCE:** core, every
  simulator target except Clique's benchmarks, and the device `w13g_probe`,
  `device` and `retained_history` targets passed 1,050 tests in 43
  binaries, with no failures, skipping those two measurement groups. The
  pre-rebase round-4 code passed 1,043 in 41.
- The only failures were four TypeScript-toolchain tests, which need the
  `node_modules` the copy lacked: three in `snapback4-lang` and `check.rs`'s
  w11r1c. The three lang tests pass here.
- `reviews.rs`, the explorer at depth 2 and the core tests pass here on the
  final tree.
## 2026-09-23 — logical expiry revokes only a grant once held live

This is a fix-forward from Astra's final review of the entry above,
`issues/20260923-snapback4-already-expired-grant-names-ids.md`. A grant
inserted with its lifetime already over used to reach its grantee twice:

- its row, re-read as absent, arrived as a `del` naming its id;
- logical expiry appended a scope naming its group.

The rule is in LLP 3000 §7.

**The fix.**

- A born row whose final image is already expired logs no put.
- `Interval` now carries its origin join and that join's explicit lifetime.
- A chain whose every join had ended by its own commit gets no
  logical-expiry scope. A span held at the watermark walks back to its last
  scope, so a live predecessor keeps its revocation. A legacy join without a
  lifetime counts as live.
- The history walk runs only on that rare path. It reads the principal's
  transitions once, groups them once, and fetches their commit times in one
  query. The common path adds no SQL.

**Review.** Astra reviewed over three rounds
(`llp/reviews/3000-already-expired-grant-names-ids.astra.md`):

- **Round 1: NOT READY.** The group leaked on the poll after the one that
  consumed the join.
- **Round 2 closed that, with no dropped revocation.** It flagged an
  O(groups × history) rare path.
- **Round 3: READY as a scoped improvement.**

**Tests.** Five `reviews.rs` cases cover the reproduction, the next poll,
snapshot then poll, a two-page catch-up, and three guards that a live grant
still revokes. One guard resumes exactly at a never-live replacement's join
with more to come. Each guard fails when the rule is loosened to the last
span or the chain walk is removed. The mutation run left a cached test
binary with the mutated walk; Astra caught it and distrusted it.

**Not fixed: the physical sweep.** A later `sweep_expired` of such a row still
logs its `del` and a scope, and the stream forwards both. Deciding that a
swept grant was never live needs the principal's log at write time.
`account_row_change` sees only `Rows`, so the ticket stays open with that
design question for the engine's owner.

**Verification.** On `expo-build-450b` (this Mac was at load 70–190), the
same targeted set as the entry above passed 1,055 tests in 43 binaries, with
no failures, skipping the device's two measurement groups: core, every
simulator target except Clique's benchmarks, and the device `w13g_probe`,
`device` and `retained_history` targets. `review_corrections` (expiring
grants), `security`, `membership`, `write_authority` and the explorer also
pass here.

## 2026-09-23 — 0.3 program: maintained columns land (F1a + F1b; LLP 3000.007.001)

`likeCount: count likes by postId` is now a maintained column. A private
maintain keeps the authoritative total, and the engine mirrors it onto live
parent rows. Adding or redefining a column over a populated store:
- rebuilds the total, and mirrors every live parent whose value differs,
  in place;
- emits no row events;
- always commits a parent-naming barrier, so devices reacquire by snapshot.

An initial zero stays absent, and reads 0. W15c's interim value-index rule
is retired. Trending is one merge over 25 lanes of
`by byHourLikes: hour(at), likeCount, at, id`. A schema with a maintained
column derives the `maintained-column` capability, which the published
0.2.33 device and engine refuse.

**Reviews.** Both families reviewed every round:

| Change | Astra | Grok |
|---|---|---|
| F1a, round 2 and finalize | READY, no findings | test-strength notes only |
| F1b | READY WITH CHANGES: one Medium, the activation clock | 22 packets |
| F1b, round 1 | READY WITH CHANGES: one Medium, fixed here | 10 packets |

F1b's round 1 did three things:
- threaded the host clock into every activation path, with a mutation proof;
- made the gate-5 harness fail closed;
- strengthened eight weak tests.

Astra's round-1 Medium was the gate-5 harness's `record()`: it asserted a
response's size before appending it to the trace, and the client swallowed
the throw, so the audit could miss an oversized response.

Every production claim in Grok's packets was checked against the code or
run, and refuted. For example, "does not compile" twice, and "17 bytes is
too small for an i53".

**F1 x F3.** The INTEGRATION lane's first Clique-shaped app failed admission.
F1a's round-2 fix had refused maintained columns on timeline-mapped tables as
well as owned ones. Only the owned half guards anything, so only owned
tables are refused now. The ruling is in LLP 3000.007.003 revision 8, §3.1.

A differential test runs the same operations on the language card's timeline
with and without counts on its mapped cards. The operations are follows,
posts, a delivered repost, votes, removal, unvote and unfollow. Every
timeline-owned row and every home page stays identical. Astra rated the
narrowing READY.

**Verification.**
- The landing suite ran on the rebased branch, with the published 0.2.33
  fence tests enabled (`SNAPBACK4_FENCE_PUBLISHED`): `cargo test` passed in 1,374 s. The client tests' only failures were four cases in one file, `wasm-codec-census`: F1b's clock threading moved the stored-schema decode from `Engine::open` into `open_at`, and the census's exception still named `open`. That is fixed, and the file passes 26/26. The published timeline, recorded-attribution and maintained-column fence tests ran against the npm artifacts and passed.
- The strengthened gate-5 harness passes at a toy size of 4,000 parents: 39
  responses, the largest 16,772,312 B, and both devices adopted with 4,000 of
  4,000 stored counts equal to 10. The full 100,000 / 1,000,000 re-run
  follows landing, before publication.
- WASM is 473,115 B gzip, within the 474,000 B ratchet.

Follow-ups, including the finding that the published-binary fence is skipped
unless its cache variable is set:
`issues/20260923-snapback4-f1-review-followups.md`.

## 2026-09-24 — LLP 3000.013 lane B: maintained views without boilerplate

Implemented on `sb4-intent/b-derived` in `9e217054c`, for supervisor review
and integration; not pushed or published. The parser admits a maintain without
a property block/read line and an in-table count/sum without `by`. The catalog
normalizes dotted group keys, derives an ordinary read declaration from the
source, and sends it through the unchanged binder, disclosure and partition
checks. A public/allow source derives allow; other rules retain every referenced
field only when it is a bare group key, including fields in probe equalities.
Missing fields refuse with E_MAINTAIN_READ_RULE. Explicit rules still win.
Maintained columns infer exactly one required or optional source reference to
the parent; zero or multiple references refuse with
E_MAINTAINED_COLUMN_REFERENCE, listing candidates and an explicit rewrite.
Both refusals have registered why text and prose on the maintains card. The
maintains and language cards compile derived-read and by-less count examples.

All nine Clique aggregates compile and run in maintain spelling, including
`count posts by parentId` as an ordinary maintain and recorded
`count posts by parentId.authorId`; no self-reference admission change was
needed. The fixture checks public scalar totals, daily groups, missing zeros,
insert/delete deltas, nested replies and credit surviving target deletion.
`posts.likeCount: count likes`, `repostCount: count reposts` and a by-less
`sum likes of .weight` use the existing private totals and mirrors. Their
write-result stripping, ownership, activation and meters are unchanged.

Residency is unchanged: without `online only`, a maintain inherits its source's
sync if the audience is public or all audience columns survive as bare group
keys. The inherited aggregate has no horizon, remains until-revoked, and does
not inherit delivered-history. No source sync or a lost audience column means
no aggregate sync (server-only). Public sources with subset delivery retain the
existing server/unknown-local completeness classification. Maintains still do
not accept a sync line of their own; private column storage never inherits sync.

Measured on the shared Linux host: the seven new regressions passed in 0.04 s.
They cover the Clique oracle; semantic identity of dotted/undotted and
explicit/inferred defaults; denied, private, calendar and path readability;
reference ambiguity, optional references and sums; unchanged residency and
admission; private snapshot/stream delivery and revocation on a real memory
Device using production sync encoding; and rule-probe extra equalities. The
existing maintains (14), maintained columns (42), recorded attribution (5) and
guide (55) tests passed. WebAssembly was 1,707,362 B raw / 472,890 B gzip against
the unchanged 474,000 B budget. `./ref-check --verbose` passed: 504 LLP docs,

## 2026-09-24 — intent lane G: per-operation scale certificates

Lane G implements the scale certificate for LLP 3000.013 on
`sb4-intent/g-scale` (implementation commit `829a21e25`). Every successful
`check` prints a scale summary. Each `check --cost` operation starts with
its verdict, while all previous cost lines remain. `check --json --cost`
adds `scale`, an array of operation certificates containing `class`,
`bounds`, `growth_sites`, `per_chunk`, `per_write` and `whole_job`, plus
`scaleSummary`. The existing human cost report remains on stderr in JSON
mode. `why <operation>` receives the same added verdict.

The analysis walks the program IR and schema, including nested shapes,
loops, lane discovery/setup, rule probes and implicit maintained reads.
It uses the engine's `scan_visibility` analysis. Residual predicates,
non-uniform read rules, uncapped domains, word expansion, expiry skips,
expiring aggregate recounts and data-derived ranges report their growth
sites and rewrites. Compiler boolean temporaries are rendered as Quarry
expressions. Jobs are assessed per chunk and name whole-sweep work
separately. Recorded attribution, maintained aggregates/columns and the
existing Following delivery cost are included in the verdict.

Engineering choices where the lane brief was silent:

- Bounds are conservative admitted meter work, with lookahead and nested
  multiplicity included. Writes use the shared runtime ceilings because
  constraints, prediction authority, derived writes and partition work
  compose with the authored writes. A failed charge may appear above those
  ceilings in a trace. No static bytes/steps admission was introduced.
- Native modules and external actions conservatively use `grows`, naming
  the absent Quarry body; this is lack of a static independence proof,
  not a measured claim that every handler scales with the corpus.
- A range depending only on arguments or the clock is independent of
  corpus size; its admitted iterations remain bounded by the step meter.
- This lane adds no Quarry grammar or refusal code. Its compiled bounds-card
  examples use the existing spellings. Predicate reads from lane A use the
  same Scan/Merge analysis, including synthesized index names. New IR from
  other lanes still needs integration: in particular, a new MergeLane
  projection must be traversed with candidate multiplicity, and streaming
  or self-chunking variants must preserve their domain's growth facts.

Measured/verified:

- `cargo test -p snapback4 --test scale`: **9 passed**, including explicit
  class pins for all 45 core language-card operations (34 constant, 11
  grows), all 11 chat operations (10 constant, external `invite` grows),
  and all 15 clique-03 operations (13 constant, `following` and `trending`
  grow because they filter removal/timestamp candidates). Jobs in these
  counts are per chunk.
- Additional certificate tests check residual versus pinned reads, uncapped
  lane discovery versus bounded lists, stored-data versus input ranges,
  hidden rows, expiring rule probes and live aggregate recounts, a schema
  cap repairing a whole-domain read, and a renamed/synthesized IR index
  with an argument page bound. CLI tests retain the old cost lines and
  verify ordinary-check summaries and structured JSON.
- Engine witnesses seed **100 then 1,200 rows** and check **pages 1–50**

- `cargo test -p snapback4 --test check`: **67 passed, 1 baseline failure**

## 2026-09-24 — intent lane G: review round 1 scale bounds

Addressed all four Astra Medium findings against the interpreter's actual
charging paths. `crates/snapback4/src/scale.rs` now allows one opening plus
up to `take` refills per merge lane, including duplicate pops in overlapping
lanes, lookahead and repeated rule evaluation. The allowance covers both
small batched merges and the one-row lazy path. Every mutation/job scan
also includes its Cut::Abort admission, including potential refills. Walks
count the seed at depth zero and share ordinary point accounting for their
rows, expiry and authorization; their nested work uses the inclusive total.

Added `src/scale/dependencies.rs`: a monotone fixed-point pass over loop
bodies, including nested IR expressions, propagates loop-carried stored-data
dependencies before the cost pass visits the body once. Dependency propagation
cannot add rows, probes or writes. A point-maintained population count passed
through `x = y; y = p` now makes a later `range(0, x)` grow with population.

structural bounds to meter ceilings, since the refused charge is recorded

allowances include a possible bulk maintain or rule reservation. Ceilings
remain unchanged in the engine and are still reported separately in JSON.

refused-charge allowances; the language card's walk comment now correctly

## 2026-09-24 — 0.4 publication fences: compatibility ruling and transactional once keys

Supervisor ruling: **a 0.4 release requires a 0.4 server**. The 0.4 compiler
may persist different selection facts, synthesized indexes and explanations.
Published 0.2.33 `serve` correctly refuses the mixed-version release with
`E_GENERATION: release source differs from its activated backend; deploy the
source as a new release`. Old devices remain compatible with capability-free
backends. The control now proves native and WASM install, adoption, queries
and persisted reopen before checking byte pins; the matching 0.4 server serves
successfully, and the old server refuses without changing the prepared
release or checkpointed store bytes.

The canonical control is 2,950 bytes, formerly 2,734. Its complete new pin
contains exactly eight diagnostic-string changes: `first 10` in the two read
sites and selected key/result/selection-reason text, each repeated in programs
and schema operation metadata. The stored-schema pin accepts precisely those
string changes against the real published encoding; no structural difference
is erased. The timeline fence now expects `timeline-v2` (LLP 3000.013 §4),
retaining old native/WASM install/adoption/reopen refusal checks.

The shared SQLite store no longer creates `_effect_keys` during open. First
use creates it inside the emitting transaction, so an outbox, heap or write
meter failure rolls back the table along with its keys. Existing lifetime
keys survive retries, reopen, replay suppression and outbox removal, as before
(LLP 3000.013 §5.3). Native and engine refusal regressions assert no new table
and unchanged raw SQLite bytes after successful opening/setup. Successful
opening of an old store may still migrate existing job-bookkeeping columns;
that setup is explicitly before the refused-adoption boundary.

Affected qualification, with the packaged SQLite build policy:
- Four real published-0.2.33 fence tests: 4 passed, 0 skipped, 3.351 s.
- Core and device suites: 253.494 s, all passed (the log records ignored cases).
- Five work-intent suites: 27 passed, 0 ignored, 21.491 s; permanent once-key
  rollback, retry, replay, reopen and outbox-removal behavior remains covered.
- CLI rebuild: 3.208 s. No ceiling or test was disabled.

Attempts remain under `reports/20260924-publication-0.4.0/`. Phase 2's dry-run
stopped on the original four client fences after 710.694 s, before staging.
Phase 3's two control probes (1.453 and 1.046 s) exposed stored-schema drift
and then the old-server refusal; the ruling above resolves that policy stop.
Phase 4 fence attempts failed at fixture initialization boundaries (8.579 s),
uncheckpointed successful-server WAL recovery (4.527 s), and Rust stored-field
order versus canonical wire order (4.600 s), before the final 4/4 pass.
The earlier append-only journal merge conflict was resolved preserving both
entries. The phase-1 push attempt failed on the root hook's missing `acorn`;
there is no further push authorization. No package has been published yet.
The changed core requires a rebuilt xcframework and renewed native evidence.

inclusive calendar range, pinned calendar key and exact time predicates.

add `snapback4 why <code>`, and omit the long explanation. Grouped multiline
notes show their one-line summary. `--verbose` keeps all member sites and
explains each code/card once, including a singleton; `why` and JSON retain
their detail. Error reporting keeps its existing behavior. Updated CLI help
and the bounds card; no new Quarry syntax or refusal code was introduced.

Added five scale tests covering hour/day/subhour recognition and conservative
fallback, per-row authorization, history versus edge density and a meter cut,
the expiry backlog counterexample, and cost text/JSON without empty rewrite
labels. Added a CLI test for repeated N_NO_HORIZON notes across plain,
verbose, why and JSON output. Updated the existing bucket, repeated-note and
grouped-maintain expectations. All 97 affected tests pass. Measured window
examined rows: 11 initially, still 11 after adding 1,000 rows outside the
window, 211 after adding 200 rejected edge rows. Adding 8,200 more edge rows
returns incomplete within the unchanged certificate allowance. Expiry reads
examine 2,001 rows before one 2,000-row sweep and one afterward, returning no
expired rows. The provided target-clique.q compiles after adding the brief's
missing `.at <= now` to Trending, and prints the 25-lane/page-10 explanation;
the integrated target's three engine tests also pass.

One requested claim was stopped: expiry is not bounded to rows expired since
the last sweep, nor to at most one second. The server checks maintenance on
a one-second tick and deletes at most 2,000 rows per pass across tables. A
burst of 2,001 expirations leaves an older row after that pass; outages,
slow maintenance and failures can leave more. Reproduce with
`cargo test -p snapback4 --test scale_windows_expiry expiry_backlog_can_outlive_one_tick_and_remains_meter_bounded -- --nocapture`.
The wording states this limit instead of inventing an age or population
guarantee. Runtime/sweep redesign was not attempted. Retaining the existing
two JSON classes and meter allowances, recognizing only proved window shapes,
and preserving grouped-note details in verbose/JSON are the implementation
choices where the brief was silent.

### 2026-09-24 — LLP 3000.013 Lane P, round 1: authorize expiry work and defer unknown cap predictions

Closed the review's premature-expiry-charge path: update/upsert targets
accumulate matching expired siblings privately and charge only after write
rule authority. Private resolution stops at the remaining examination
allowance plus one; unresolved update/delete returns the ordinary NOT_FOUND,
and an upsert cannot insert without paying that over-ceiling debt. This keeps
both denied-world logical observations and physical resolution bounded.
Alternate-key delete now uses an engine-private DeleteTarget with its existing
read/delete gates, instead of a generated public Get before authorization.
The original by-id Delete IR remains compatible. Denied update, upsert,
insert-if-absent and both delete addresses have identical complete refusals and
meters with zero versus 9,000 expired siblings.

Devices now queue occupancy-increasing writes on expiring capped tables:
even complete live snapshots omit unswept physical rows. Memory and SQLite
adapters persist those queues without predicted rows across reopen, settle
server cap refusals, and acquire successful replacements after sweeping. A
queued send rolls back its earlier conversation update too. Same-group
updates/upserts, deletes and same-id expired replacements with held
predecessors retain prediction; cap-group moves defer.

Secondary collision cleanup deliberately remains with the background sweep,
as permitted by the review. The never-live-grant disclosure regression still
passes. A replacement at a full cap refuses with a write site and a rewrite
naming the one-second tick and maximum 2,000-row pass. No lifecycle/provenance
redesign, new Quarry spelling or new refusal code was added.

Measured: 21 expiry regressions and 25 existing disclosure reviews passed.
9,000 sends still examine exactly one row apiece with either zero or 3,000
unrelated expired rows. The 5,000-sibling upsert reaches E_BOUND at 8,193;
removing target accumulation made that regression fail with an incorrect
5,001-examination commit. The production charge was restored. The old binder
